beats.en: A tirtha is a holy place, literally a crossing place, a ford where one crosses over. In the Jain tradition a tirtha is linked to places where the Tirthankaras attained liberation or where major events of their lives

textbookBox.concept: Each shrine has its own mythology. A legend tells of Shiva carrying the body of Sati in grief, and her body parts fell in many places that became Shakti Peethas.

beats.en: Each shrine has its own mythology. A legend tells of Shiva carrying the body of Sati in grief, and her body parts fell in many places that became Shakti Peethas. Such stories link far-off places into networks.
beats.speakEn: Each shrine has its own mythology. A legend tells of Shiva carrying the body of Sati in grief, and her body parts fell in many places that became Shakti Peethas. Such stories link far-off places into networks.

beats.en: The Nadistuti Sukta of the Rig Veda praises rivers and invokes 19 major rivers of ancient northwest India. Rivers such as the Ganga are worshipped as mothers.
beats.speakEn: The Nadistuti Sukta of the Rig Veda praises rivers and invokes 19 major rivers of ancient northwest India. Rivers such as the Ganga are worshipped as mothers.
